claim: The two JAMBU tables trace to the same upstream, the DSAL online DEDR, and are therefore one source and not two. dedr.csv comes from a SQL database scraped from the online version in October 2013, which JAMBU marks deprecated; dedr_new.csv comes from parse.py scraping dsal.uchicago.edu over 514 pages.
locator: JAMBU README lines 135 and 137; data/dedr/parse.py lines 36 (TOTAL_PAGES = 514), 173 (burrow_query.py) and 155 (output dedr_new.csv)
notes: Constitution step 5. Recorded in 02-SOURCES/dependency.csv as DEP-025. The consequence is that the two tables agreeing is not confirmation of anything about Burrow and Emeneau; it is a statement about the stability of one website between 2013 and 2026.

claim: Within that single DSAL lineage the two scrapes disagree on 5.5% of entry-language assignments across the 18 languages whose labels map one-to-one, against the 10.3% IC-E-001 measures between the DSAL lineage and the digitization MelaKeela ships.
locator: 04-AUDITS/dedr-lineage-check.py, output 04-AUDITS/dedr-lineage-check.csv; same 18-language mapping and same method as 04-AUDITS/domain-e-dedr-digitisation-check.py
notes: Per language the within-lineage rate runs 2.0% (Tamil) to 14.3% (Kolami). This makes the error bar on any DEDR-derived count WORSE, not better: roughly half of the disagreement IC-E-001 attributes to two digitizations is present between two parses of the identical source pages, so it is parse noise rather than disagreement about the dictionary. Kolami is the worst cell on both comparisons (14.3% here, 19.7% in IC-E-001).

claim: The Brahui-with-a-Tamil-cognate figure is 220 of 269 (82%) on the 2013 DSAL scrape and 223 of 273 (82%) on the 2026 one. The site publishes 191 of 262 (73%).
locator: 04-AUDITS/dedr-lineage-check.py; the site figures are as recorded in 04-AUDITS/domain-e-dedr-digitisation-check.csv, last row

claim: The 10.3% of IC-E-001 is a disagreement between two independent readings of Burrow and Emeneau.
notes: The reading IC-E-001's wording invites and that D-038 is framed on. It requires DEDR-L-005 to be closed in one direction. The rival, equally untested, is that ArimeKannada is itself DSAL-derived and the 10.3% is one digitization's parse noise compounded. Recorded as a HYPOTHESIS so that neither is asserted in the interim, and so that D-038's options are not read as resting on a settled fact.
